articles.author: LLMCoder
articles.description:
Claude Code is a terminal agent that speaks the Anthropic Messages API. LM Studio is a desktop app that serves local models over an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Both look like "an API on localhost", so the obvious move is to point one at the other — and it does not work. Not because of a setting you missed: the two speak different protocols.
Here is what actually breaks, and the two ways to bridge it.
LM Studio exposes POST /v1/chat/completions with OpenAI's request shape and OpenAI's response shape. Claude Code sends POST /v1/messages with Anthropic's shape and expects Anthropic's event stream back. There is no flag on either side that makes them agree, because the disagreement is in the payload, not in the URL.
The second thing that breaks is the model name. Claude Code resolves the model…
articles.title: Running a local model from LM Studio inside Claude Code: what actually breaks

But the default quickstart is not a production setup. This is the setup I run in production, and the one I would defend in a DevOps interview.

articles.description:
A repository file should not be able to choose the Git LFS transfer command


Git LFS is designed to fetch large objects without asking the developer to think about transport details. CVE-2026-105803 affects versions 3.0.0 through 3.8.0 and is fixed in 3.8.1. A malicious repository can use an .lfsconfig file to supply a configuration key that Git LFS fails to restrict correctly, causing it to invoke an attacker-controlled command or binary during object fetch.
An .lfsconfig file belongs to the repository. It is useful for project-level settings, but it must not be treated as local trust. The advisory says Git LFS permits only a limited set of configuration options from that file and failed to filter keys with additional components. The attacker can mimic an option that selects a custom obj…
